niche: a Spanish home-workout subscription app placing each of its seven paid acquisition channels in the growth policy's scale, hold or cut band for 2027, on the 12-month net revenue per euro that the 2027 media plan's weekly spend on each channel buys
answer: scale Apple Search Ads; hold Meta iOS, Meta Android, Google Android and AppLovin Android; cut TikTok iOS and TikTok Android (2027 return per euro at the plan's weekly spend: Apple Search Ads 1.48; Meta iOS 1.04, Meta Android 1.08, Google Android 1.06, AppLovin Android 0.94; TikTok iOS 0.78, TikTok Android 0.72); three stumps, five open channels, eleven shortcut routes on eleven distinct wrong calls
analyst_test: A careful but hurried analyst values each channel on the app's own payment records and scales every user's revenue by the stores' total over the app's (the gap spread in proportion to what was recorded), reads the iOS ad channels on the users the attribution export holds, and carries each channel's 2026 revenue per euro to the 2027 plan's spend; that route scales Meta iOS and TikTok iOS, scales Google Android and cuts AppLovin, against the golden's hold, cut, hold and hold.
domain_test: Each result is an acquisition-economics and lifetime-value quantity of a subscription app (installs by channel from the instrument that sees them, the store charges the app never recorded, each channel's 12-month net revenue per install and per euro at a weekly spend); swap the nouns for another field's and the store reports, conversion values and tracking consent stop making sense.

world.org_type: a home-workout and yoga subscription app

driver: Each channel's band rests on what a euro of its 2027 spend returns in twelve months, a quantity no record holds: the app's own records hold only the store charges a user's next open showed it, the attribution export holds only the iOS users who allowed tracking, and the plan buys some channels at weekly spends where the auction charges more and returns weaker users; each part of the estimand is read from the instrument that sees it (the stores' sales reports for the charges, the ad networks' conversion postbacks for the iOS installs, the 2026 weeks of heavier spend for the response).
driver_concrete: Zancada's growth policy places a paid channel in scale, hold or cut on its 12-month net revenue per euro at the 2027 plan's weekly spend (1.20 and 0.90 the lines). Subscribers who stop opening the app keep paying for months and the app records none of it, so the stores' reports exceed the app's records by about a fifth, unevenly by channel (a third of AppLovin's revenue); iOS users who allow tracking are the more engaged (Meta iOS's consenting users bring about 40 per cent more per install than its installs as a whole); and the plan raises Google Android's weekly spend by about 70 per cent, where its 2026 pushes show dearer and weaker installs.
stump: The careful but hurried route (the app's records scaled to the stores' totals in proportion, the attribution export's iOS users, 2026 revenue per euro carried to the plan) files Meta iOS and TikTok iOS scale, Google Android scale and AppLovin cut against the golden's hold, cut, hold and hold; reading the app's records raw cuts Meta iOS, Meta Android, Google Android and AppLovin instead.
results: R1 2026 installs and cost per install by channel from the instrument that sees each; R2 the store charges and net revenue the app never recorded, by channel; R3 the iOS ad channels' 12-month net revenue per install over all their installs; R4 Google Android's installs and 12-month net revenue per install at the plan's weekly spend; R5 each channel's 12-month net revenue per euro at the plan's spend; R6 each channel's band
one_fact_test: the recording sentence (a store charge reaches the app's records only at the user's next open) rescues R2 and AppLovin's band (2 of 6); the consent sentence rescues R3 and the two iOS bands' direction (1 of 6 results); the response sentence R4 (1 of 6)

differentiation.mark115: mark115 forecast a deal mechanic's second response where its new level crosses a rival's, measured on the stores that moved; here no response at a rival's level decides anything: each channel's 12-month return is assembled from three instruments with their own blind spots (store charges the app sees only at the user's next open, iOS installs the attribution export sees only with tracking consent, a spend response seen only in the 2026 pushes), each opening a different channel
